text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate observed for /v1/generate in eu-west-2 (~80-90% 5xx, elevated latencies). Auto-created incident channel #incidents. Severity: P1. Runbook: inference-availability -> network-degradation.

devon: taking this (oncall). starting quick triage. Can someone confirm if Dedicated pools show similar errors?

mike: checking dedicated nodes now — metrics look normal for dedicated, errors concentrated on hosted pool in eu-west-2.

alice: seeing huge TCP retransmits on the NICs for inference-worker-* in eu-west-2. rx_kbps ~ saturated, tx ~ normal.

devon: digging into NLB logs and target group healthchecks. If it's ENI-level packet drops we may need cross-zone routing now.

ops-bot: autopage to netinfra team @netops sent. Scheduled fix window: immediate mitigation steps in runbook.

lee: FYI Route53 health checks for the regional endpoint are flapping — latency and failed connections.

devon: commands i'm running:```ssh admin@inference-worker-47
sudo tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
sudo ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "rx_|tx_"
curl -sv https://internal-health/eu-west-2/generate 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'```

alice: paste from ethtool: `rx_packets: 1.2e9, rx_errors: 0, rx_dropped: 13400, rx_over_errors: 0, rx_fifo_errors: 0` — but kernel counters show high requeues and retransmits.

mike: NLB logs show many connections reset with `RST` and `503` from origin. Backend connection errors spike at 15:03 UTC.

devon: probable ENI contention / hypervisor host network saturation in a subset of AZ. Need to confirm instance-level vs AZ-wide.

lee: looking at EC2 metrics — a set of instances in eu-west-2a show NIC TX queue length skyrocketing and ENI detach/re-attach events around 15:02. That matches the error window.

sara: customer impact — we see degraded latencies and 5xx for ~12% of total US+EU hosted traffic routed to eu-west-2. Premium Dedicated customers unaffected. Preparing status page note draft.

devon: mitigation plan (short): 1) enable cross-zone load balancing on NLB to redistribute away from impacted hosts 2) route DNS to eu-west-1 failover for new traffic (low TTL) 3) scale up eu-west-2 replacement fleet in unaffected AZs and move warm model-caches over 4) temporarily enable model fallback to quantized variant to reduce per-token token processing CPU+network pressure.

mike: applying cross-zone load balancer setting now. patching target group config to enable cross-zone:```aws elbv2 modify-load-balancer-attributes --load-balancer-arn <nlb-arn> --attributes Key=load_balancing.cross_zone.enabled,Value=true```

devon: lowering Route53 TTL for service record and initiating failover weight shift to eu-west-1:```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch file://failover-eu.json``` (failover file adds weight 80 to eu-west-1).

ops-bot: Runbook step executed: start draining targets in eu-west-2a. Use drain timeout 90s to preserve in-flight requests where possible.

alice: starting controlled drain on affected instances. command: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn <tg> --targets Id=i-0abc` (done for 6 instances). Observed immediate drop in errors for those targets in NLB logs.

devon: spinning up replacement fleet in eu-west-2b/c with instance type g5.xlarge (same AMI). Launch config changes: bump autoscale min by +8, warm cache bootstrap jobs enqueued.

mike: temporary SDK mitigation: pushing config to increase client retries and small backoff: set retries=3, backoff=200ms. Not ideal but reduces surface during switchover.

lee: RFC: should we enable accelerated DNS failover to eu-west-1 for ALL traffic until full verification? risk: slightly higher latencies for EU customers but avoids errors.

devon: agree. set weight now and monitor errors for 10m. If stable, keep until replacement fleet healthy.

sara: drafting status page: "We are experiencing degraded availability for hosted inference in eu-west-2; a subset of network interfaces in one AZ experienced heavy packet loss causing request errors. Dedicated customers unaffected. Engineers are mitigating by draining affected hosts, redistributing traffic, and launching replacement capacity."

devon: monitoring p99 latency, 5xx rate now trending down from 85% to 12% for eu-west-2 origin after drains and cross-zone. Good signs.

alice: still seeing a small cohort of ENI re-attach logs — might be underlying host NIC driver bug triggered under burst. Need postmortem.

mike: alerting oncall for next 4h handoff: lee, please take second shift and coordinate with netops for hypervisor host remediation.

lee: taking incident for next shift. I'll coordinate kernel/firmware checks with netops and schedule a rolling host reboot if needed. Also will run packet captures to confirm root cause.

ops-bot: handoff recorded. oncall -> lee.

devon: preparing brief for postmortem: timeline, impact (approx 12% hosted traffic degraded for ~45m, peak 15:02-15:40 UTC), mitigation steps, and long-term mitigation: 1) proactively enable cross-AZ distribution for NLBs; 2) add ENI saturation alarms; 3) automated DNS failover playbook test; 4) bake model-fallback into serving config.

sara: posted status update. Notifying top 10 customers impacted and offering SLA credits as per playbook.

alice: collected debug bundle (dmesg, ethtool, netstat, tcpdump snippets) and uploaded to perf-buckets/inference/eu-west-2/1778001234-debug.tgz.

lee: I'll follow up with a run of the host firmware audit and schedule reboots in rolling fashion across the AZ tomorrow 02:00 UTC if netops approves.

devon: closing active mitigation; monitoring for 30m. If errors remain below 1% for 30m we mark status as "degraded - recovering" then "resolved". Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity downgraded to P2. Next: postmortem assigned to devon + alice + netops.

devon: assigning postmortem owners and initial draft to be ready EOD tomorrow.

lee: acknowledged, taking on-call.

end of thread.
